meaning: Titles and reading notes drafted by an AI agent in the register of the paper they annotate. No mathematician has reviewed them.

notes.Breakdown.AdjointDefect.AdjointDefectBou: The centre and free-direction estimates hold uniformly for α∈K; one family of free-direction dual bounds must work for every α. Their total, including the pin contribution, must be at most aⱼ.
notes.Breakdown.AdjointDefect.AdjointDefectEnt: Parameter directions can receive separate potential estimates or share weighted norm estimates. In the final cell certificate every direction uses the latter option.
The adjoint transport uses the centre field at α and the fixed central period; dependence on α can still enter through the radial phase.

The total contains the centre potential contribution, coordinate-weighted fitted contributions and a weighted Cauchy–Schwarz bound for the remaining directions. The fitted sum vanishes in the final cell construction.
For a fitted direction, the residual adds the adjoint advection contribution and subtracts the reciprocal-period rate times ∂θψ.
The pin contribution is n_Φ+n_Yc_Ξ/√w_*, separating the potential error from the gradient approximation error.
The flux is ∇ψ−ΣₗYⱼₗ(∇Φ̃ₗ−(∇Φ̃ₗ)ᵀ). Divergence freedom of the generators is used later when the divergence of this antisymmetric correction is expanded.
notes.Breakdown.AdjointDefect.AzimuthalBounded: The finite expansion uses distinct triples of component, time frequency and azimuthal order, with measurable amplitudes and spatial almost-everywhere equality at each time. Its weighted estimate uses (|m|+1/2)⁻² and the circular-component factors 1/2, 1/2 and 1.
notes.Breakdown.AdjointDefect.DualBounded: One decomposition R=R₁+R₂ must satisfy both the azimuthal and Hardy estimates, with the two nonnegative bounds adding to at most ρ.
notes.Breakdown.AdjointDefect.PinData: The two supplied families represent pin potentials Φₗ and generators Φ̃ₗ. Compact support and divergence freedom are established by the later conditions on these fields.
notes.Breakdown.AdjointDefect.PotentialData: The four supplied fields are the vector potentials G and U, the matrix potential F and the scalar pressure correction q. Their regularity and size bounds are imposed separately.
notes.Breakdown.AdjointDefect.PotentialNorms: All four proposed bounds must be nonnegative, and the period integrals of |G|², |∇U|² and |F|² must lie below their squared bounds. The remaining dual estimate is a separate condition on the residual.
notes.Breakdown.AdjointDefect.PotentialNumbers: The four proposed numbers control G, ∇U, F and the dual remainder separately; their validity is established by the corresponding norm and remainder inequalities.
notes.Breakdown.AdjointDefect.RemainderBounded: The condition requires a measurable field and ρ≥0 with ∫₀¹∫|y|²|R|²≤(ρ/2)². The factor 2 is the Hardy constant used to turn this weighted bound into a dual estimate.
notes.Breakdown.AdjointDefect.adjointTransport: The transport expression is −S⁻¹∂θψ−ψ−(y·∇)ψ/2+(∇W)ᵀψ−(W·∇)ψ, with each sign fixed before adding the diffusion and potential terms.
notes.Breakdown.AdjointDefect.advectionShift: The two terms are (∇δ)ᵀψ and −(δ·∇)ψ, with the transpose acting on ψ in the first term.
notes.Breakdown.AdjointDefect.axisRotation: Rotation through α acts on the first two Cartesian coordinates and fixes the vertical coordinate; these rotations determine the azimuthal transformation law of each amplitude.
notes.Breakdown.AdjointDefect.complexComponent: The three scalar components are R₁+iR₂, R₁−iR₂ and R₃. The first two are circular combinations of Cartesian components.
notes.Breakdown.AdjointDefect.componentWeight: The circular components have squared-norm weight 1/2 each and the vertical component has weight 1, recovering the ordinary vector norm.
notes.Breakdown.AdjointDefect.matrixDivergence: For a matrix field K, the divergence used here is Σᵢ(∂ᵢK)eᵢ. This fixes the component order when identifying the matrix potential with the paper's div Fᵀ.
notes.Breakdown.AdjointDefect.potentialDefect: The combined potential contribution is √(n_G²+(w_*n_U+n_F+n_R)²/w_*), the first contribution in (B.53).
notes.Breakdown.AdjointDefect.remainderField: The remainder is the transport field minus the pin-flux divergence, plus ∇q+∆G+w_*∆U−div Fᵀ, using the same matrix component convention throughout.
notes.Breakdown.AdjointDefect.secondDeriv: The spatial Hessian is obtained by differentiating the gradient; its diagonal trace gives the Laplacian in the adjoint residual.
notes.Breakdown.AdjointDefect.timeDerivative: The derivative is ∂θ at fixed spatial position, where θ has period one; the adjoint equation supplies the factor 1/S separately.
notes.Breakdown.AdjointDefect.transposeApply: The i-th component of Kᵀz is ⟨Keᵢ,z⟩, so the sum over the three coordinate vectors is the usual transpose action.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.CellBase: The data give real monomial coefficients for radial and height polynomials at every nonnegative degree. A finite representation must specify how these coefficient families continue beyond its stored range.
The height polynomial is ∑ᵢ₌₀ˡ bₗᵢzⁱ. Orthonormality and the positive leading coefficient are separate requirements on the family.
The radial polynomial is ∑ᵢ₌₀ʲ aⱼᵢrⁱ, so its degree is at most j. The separate positive-leading-coefficient condition makes the degree exactly j.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.CellBox: The four numbers are the radial and height endpoints of a meridian rectangle. Its geometric validity is imposed separately by 0≤r₁<r₂ and 0≤z₁<z₂.
A rectangle meets the axis precisely when its inner radial endpoint satisfies r₁=0.
The derivative is ∂P(r,z)/∂z, with r held fixed. The function may be complex-valued.
The lower radial comparison factor is 1 on an axis cell and r₁ on an off-axis cell, following the convention of (B.27).
The radial polynomial measure has weight r on axis cells and weight 1 on cells separated from the axis. This is the Jacobi and Legendre distinction used in (B.27).
The two-dimensional basis weight depends only on r: it is r for an axis cell and 1 for an off-axis cell.
The weighted square is ∫_Q m|F|² dr dz. A nonnegative weight is needed for its interpretation as a squared seminorm.
The weighted pairing is ∫_Q m F conjugate(P) dr dz, with conjugation on the test function.

The selected polynomial has a residual orthogonal to every polynomial within the prescribed degree bounds. If no such polynomial exists, the formula gives zero; the analytic projection arguments establish the appropriate existence and uniqueness.
The derivative is ∂ᵣP(r,z), with z held fixed. Its use as a classical derivative requires the appropriate differentiability of P.
The meridian set is the closed rectangle [r₁,r₂]×[z₁,z₂]. Shared sides therefore remain in both adjoining rectangles.
The radial reference coordinate is (2r−r₁−r₂)/(r₂−r₁). Positive cell width makes it the affine map from [r₁,r₂] onto [−1,1].
The height reference coordinate is (2z−z₁−z₂)/(z₂−z₁). The ordered height endpoints give the usual orientation from −1 to 1.
The associated solid consists of points with r₁≤r≤r₂ and z₁≤|z|≤z₂. It includes all azimuthal angles and both reflected halves.
The tail square is the weighted integral of |F−Π_QF|², where the projection includes degree Q in both meridian variables.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.CellScal: The data specify polynomial cutoffs, resolved angular modes, the local 12×12 form, and the losses assigned to unresolved terms. In the time-periodic construction the corresponding choices are made for each space-time harmonic.

The measure ratio is r divided by the radial polynomial weight. It equals 1 for r>0 on an axis cell and takes the prescribed value 0 at r=0; the endpoint does not change integrals with respect to area measure.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.IsCellBa: Both polynomial families have positive leading coefficients at every degree. Their inner products are Kronecker deltas, using the axis-dependent radial measure and ordinary height measure.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.IsCellBo: The geometric requirements are 0≤r₁<r₂ and 0≤z₁<z₂. They exclude zero-width cells and justify the reference-coordinate denominators.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.angularU: The azimuthal unit vector is eφ=(−sinφ,cosφ,0), the angular derivative of eᵣ.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.axialUni: The axial unit vector is e_z=(0,0,1), independent of the spatial angle.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.azimuth: The angular frequency is κn for an integer n and symmetry order κ. This preliminary construction has one frequency index; the time-periodic construction uses a pair.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.curlComp: The curl component is the contraction ∑ⱼₗ εᵢⱼₗ sₗⱼ. Thus the first index of s is the vector component and the second is the differentiation direction.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.curlSq: The curl square is the sum of the three squared moduli after antisymmetric contraction of the gradient. The three curl components determine this quantity.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.cylHeigh: The height is the signed third Cartesian coordinate z. Reflection to nonnegative height is a separate operation.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.cylPoint: The coordinate map sends (r,φ,z) to (r cosφ,r sinφ,z). Here φ denotes the spatial angle, as in the paper.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.cylRadiu: The cylindrical radius is r=√(y₁²+y₂²), using the two horizontal Cartesian components.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.heightEi: The height eigenvalue is l(l+1)[2/(z₂−z₁)]². In particular, the constant height polynomial has eigenvalue zero.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.pairVec: The 12 coordinates list the nine gradient components in row order, followed by the three velocity components. This fixes the ordering in the local matrices of (B.26).
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.polyFn: The polynomial space consists of complex functions with degree at most d in r and at most d′ in z. Its description is by the existence of a finite coefficient expansion.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.radialEi: The radial eigenvalue is j(j+2)[2/(r₂−r₁)]² on axis cells and j(j+1)[2/(r₂−r₁)]² off the axis. Both give zero at j=0.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.radialUn: The radial unit vector is eᵣ=(cosφ,sinφ,0) in Cartesian coordinates.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.sesqValu: The local value is Re(U*AU) on the 12 gradient-and-velocity coordinates, with conjugation on the first factor.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.sumSq: The gradient square is ∑ₐᵦ|sₐᵦ|² over all nine complex entries.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.supremum: The stretching majorant is λ|curl G|²+√(7/2)g₀|G||v|+√(7/2)g′(ℓ|G|²+|v|²/ℓ)/2. The balancing length must be positive in the estimates that use it.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellCoordinates.MeshS: The reconstructed segment preserves its face coordinate, interval, and test family, while choosing an auxiliary opposite coordinate one unit away. This auxiliary choice need not equal a physical cell width.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellCoordinates.Skele: A shared boundary coordinate is identified by its harmonic, geometric segment or corner, component, and complete polynomial test data. Coordinates internal to a cell carry a separate designation.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellCoordinates.keyOf: The boundary identifier retains the full test family and geometric location of each side or corner quantity. Volume and auxiliary whole-side coefficients remain internal.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.LowIndex: The data locate gradient and velocity coefficients in a common coordinate vector and supply radial- and height-face moment rows. The gradient degrees run through Q, while the velocity degrees are below Q.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.LowSlot: A low polynomial coordinate belongs either to a gradient component with degrees through Q or to a velocity component with degrees below Q.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.angularArr: For a chosen linear combination of gradient entries, the angular coefficient array is obtained by summing the frequency and two frame-rotation contributions for each entry.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.angularAxi: The angular form on axis cells uses the r-weighted Gram matrix of axis-compatible tests. Its bounds come from their pairings with the known coefficients.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.angularCom: The angular derivative of a gradient component contains the frequency term ik and frame-rotation terms in both component indices.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.angularOff: The off-axis angular form adds the diagonal contribution 1/r₂ to a remainder obtained from tests weighted by (r₂−r)/(rr₂).
The off-axis angular weight is (r₂−r)/(rr₂). It is nonnegative on a valid off-axis interval and vanishes at r₂.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.angularTes: The axis-compatible angular test is r^(j+1)zˡ, obtained by multiplying the meridian monomial by r.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.basisFn: The two-variable basis function is the product pⱼ(r)qₗ(z). The separate basis conditions determine its normalization.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.componentF: The component energy adds radial, height, and angular contributions. Axis cells omit the off-axis interior terms and use the axis-compatible angular tests.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.curlArray: The coefficient array uses the alternating symbol to extract one curl component from the gradient, with the differentiation index in the second gradient position.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.energyForm: For each mode, the form adds weighted gradient and curl derivative energies and subtracts the designated highest-degree penalty. The result is then summed over the resolved modes.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.formOfRows: If R is the matrix of rows, the form on the original coordinates is R*GR. Complex conjugation falls on the first row factor.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.frameTurn: The frame-rotation matrix has the two nonzero entries corresponding to ∂φeᵣ=eφ and ∂φeφ=−eᵣ.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.heightFace: The height-face row combines the component traces with the same coefficient array and the height-face test index.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.heightInne: The height interior form uses the differentiated weighted tests and their Gram matrix, with both test degrees below Q.
The interior height weight is (r−r₁)(1−η²), where η is the height reference coordinate.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.heightMome: The height moment is ∫zˡqₗ′(z)dz over the height interval.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.heightOute: The outer height form uses the inverse Gram matrix with cylindrical weight r and test degrees through q radially and through Q vertically.
The outer height row combines the two height-face moments with the negative height derivative of rηrʲzˡ in the interior.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.heightProj: The known height derivative energy uses the same low coefficients and radial comparison factor, with the height derivative and factor 1−η².
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.heightSlop: This derivative is ∂zf(r,z) for a real test f, with radius fixed.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.layoutInde: The chosen cell layout supplies the low-coefficient locations and the trace rows. Its four faces are ordered as two radial faces followed by two height faces.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.lowPairRow: The test pairing sums the known gradient coefficients against the integrals of the test times the tensor-product basis functions.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.lowRow: At a fixed harmonic and polynomial index, the row is the chosen linear combination of gradient coordinates.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.matrixSesq: The paired local form is U*AU′ on two 12-component vectors. This expression remains complex-valued until a real part is explicitly taken.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.monomial: The monomial is rʲzˡ in the physical meridian coordinates. Cell-model coefficients expressed in affine coordinates use a different evaluation formula.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.radialFace: The radial-face row combines the nine component trace rows with the supplied coefficient array, allowing either gradient or curl combinations.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.radialInne: The radial interior form uses integration by parts and the inverse test Gram matrix, with radial degrees below Q−1 and height degrees through Q. This family is empty when Q≤1.
The interior radial weight is (r−r₁)(1−ξ²), where ξ is the radial reference coordinate.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.radialMome: The radial moment is ∫w(r)rʲpⱼ′(r)dr, with w(r)=r on axis cells and w(r)=1 elsewhere.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.radialOute: The outer radial derivative form pairs these boundary rows through the inverse Gram matrix with cylindrical measure r dr dz.
The outer radial row combines both face moments with the interior derivative of rξ times the weighted test. The endpoint values ξ=−1 and ξ=1 account for the two positive face terms.
The outer radial test is w(r)rʲzˡ, where w is the axis-dependent polynomial measure.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.radialProj: The known radial derivative energy is a quadratic form in the low polynomial coefficients. Its integral contains the radial measure, the lower radial comparison factor, and 1−ξ² in the reference coordinate.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.radialSlop: This derivative is ∂ᵣf(r,z) for a real test f, with height fixed.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.rectIntegr: The integral is over the meridian rectangle with measure dr dz. A radial weight must be included explicitly in the integrand.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.slotIndex: The selected gradient or velocity coefficient is placed in the common data vector using the appropriate coordinate map.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.slotRow: The row reads one low coefficient at its harmonic and component-degree position, taking value 1 there and 0 elsewhere.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.slotValue: A single low coordinate represents one tensor-product basis function in its chosen component. The other components and the other field, velocity or gradient, are zero.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.testInnerM: The test Gram matrix has entries ∫_Q mPᵢPⱼ dr dz. Its entries are real, even when the matrix is subsequently used on complex coordinates.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.testSupFor: The test form is R*G⁻¹R for the matrix R of test rows. Positive definiteness of G is required when interpreting this expression as the optimal bound from those tests.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.topForm: The penalty selects the upper polynomial-degree strips in the radial and height columns of the gradient. When Q=0, the lower threshold Q−1 is taken to be zero.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.unitArray: The coefficient array equals 1 at the chosen ordered pair of gradient indices and 0 elsewhere.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.CellDatum: The eight coordinate families distinguish volume gradients, volume velocities, side velocities, side gradients, pressure moments, corner velocities, corner stream values, and whole-side velocities. Only the stream-value family has no harmonic index.
There is one stream-function coordinate per represented corner, independent of the number of harmonics.
A corner-velocity coordinate identifies one component of one harmonic at a represented corner. The geometry determines which corners require such coordinates.
An auxiliary side-velocity coordinate identifies one of the four cell sides, a harmonic, a component, and a test degree from 0 through Q.
A gradient coordinate is specified by a harmonic, two component indices, and two polynomial degrees from 0 through Q.
A velocity coordinate is specified by a harmonic, one component, and two polynomial degrees strictly below Q.
A side-gradient coordinate uses test degrees from 0 through q, one degree fewer than the side-velocity family.
A side-velocity coordinate contains a harmonic, segment, component, and test degree from 0 through q+1.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.CellLayou: The cell coordinates include volume coefficients, side and pressure moments, corner values, and auxiliary whole-side moments. The validity conditions specify when an axis corner is omitted.
The eight coordinate families use the harmonic set, polynomial degrees, segment counts, and corner count of the chosen cell layout.
Boundary coordinates comprise side velocity, side gradient, pressure moments, corner velocity, and corner stream values. Volume coefficients and auxiliary whole-side moments lie outside this set.
The ten relation families separate derivative identities, divergence, axis identities, stream identities, and compatibility of side moments. Each family retains its own degree ranges.
The corner row reads the selected velocity component when that corner is represented and gives zero for an omitted corner. The layout conditions control the axis omissions.
The auxiliary whole-side row selects the requested coefficient through degree Q and vanishes for larger degrees.

Gradient traces are recovered by tangential integration by parts, the angular frequency and frame terms, or the supplied normal-derivative moments. The chosen formula depends on the face and differentiation direction.
The height integral uses ordinary dz on [z₁,z₂]. Including the endpoints adds no mass.
The height derivative entry pairs a differentiated height polynomial with another basis polynomial, multiplied by 1−η² in the height reference coordinate.
Equality of two cell coordinates means equality of their family and all its indices. This logical identification supplies no prescribed comparison algorithm for a certificate file.
The cell coordinate set is finite because each of its eight families has finitely many indices. A file representation still needs an explicit correspondence with these coordinates.
The radial integration test is r^(i+2) on an axis cell and rⁱ off the axis. The shifted powers enforce the axis-compatible boundary identities.
The radial integral uses ordinary dr on [r₁,r₂]. Any cylindrical or polynomial weight appears in the integrand.
Multiplication by r has matrix entries ∫w(r)r pᵢ(r)pⱼ(r)dr in the radial basis.
The radial derivative entry pairs a differentiated radial polynomial with another basis polynomial, using the radial measure and the factor 1−ξ² in the reference coordinate.

The ten linear relation families express derivative, divergence, axis, stream, and side-moment identities. Zero-degree and absent-mode cases can give zero rows, so the selected elimination block must be checked separately for invertibility.
The segment pairing integrates the supplied test times the segment polynomial over that segment's tangential interval.
The whole-side gradient moment is the sum of the segment moments, weighted by the pairings of the whole-side test with each segment test.
For height sides, side 2 selects the lower endpoint and side 3 selects the upper endpoint.
For radial sides, side 0 selects the inner endpoint and side 1 selects the outer endpoint.
The inner radial side has radius r₁ and the outer radial side has radius r₂. The formula is used in the radial-side cases.
A radial face uses a height basis polynomial. A height face uses a radial basis polynomial, multiplied by r when the cell touches the axis.
The whole-side velocity moment combines the moments on its segments using test degrees from 0 through q+1.
The gradient row selects the specified coefficient when both degrees are at most Q and is zero outside that range.
On each face, the normal diagonal gradient entry is replaced by minus the other two diagonal entries. This enforces zero divergence in the reconstructed trace.
A represented corner contributes its stream-function coordinate. An omitted corner contributes zero; valid geometry limits this case to the permitted axis endpoint.
For angular frequency k, the angular velocity derivatives are ikvᵣ−vφ, ikvφ+vᵣ, and ikv_z. The extra terms arise from rotation of the cylindrical frame.
The angular derivative of a side moment combines ik times that moment with the cylindrical-frame corrections −vφ and +vᵣ in the first two components.
The coordinate row is 1 at the selected coordinate and 0 elsewhere, so pairing it with a data vector reads that entry.
The velocity row selects the specified coefficient when both degrees are below Q and is zero otherwise.
The zero angular mode is available precisely when 0 belongs to the selected mode set. Axis and stream relations use this membership test.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.FaceSegme: A side segment specifies its direction, trace and opposite coordinates, tangential interval, and polynomial tests. The opposite coordinate determines the strip used to recover the trace.
The trace formula chooses the radial or height strip according to the face direction. The extra cylindrical weight r is inserted only in the height-strip case when requested.
The degree-d test is the sum of its coefficients through degree d. The family includes a test for every nonnegative integer d.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.IsCellLay: The layout must match the given cell, modes, degrees, and orthonormal bases, with correctly placed segments and corners. Its conditions also require side coverage, disjoint segment interiors, and the stated axis exceptions.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.IsCellPar: Every selected elimination row must be one of the exact cell relations, and every retained boundary coordinate must belong to an allowed boundary family. The selected solved block must have nonzero determinant.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.IsFaceSeg: The opposite coordinate must differ from the trace coordinate, the tangential interval must have positive length, and every test polynomial must have nonzero leading coefficient.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.IsParamDa: The solved coordinates must be distinct, disjoint from the retained boundary coordinates, and give a matrix with nonzero determinant. Other unsolved coordinates may still lie outside the retained boundary set.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.ParamData: The elimination data specify the relation matrix, one coordinate to solve for in each selected row, and retained boundary coordinates. Invertibility of the solved block is a separate requirement.
The solved block takes, in every relation row, the columns named as solved coordinates. It is square because there is one such column per selected relation.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.edgeSign: The face orientation is +1 when the opposite coordinate is smaller and −1 otherwise. Valid face geometry ensures that the two coordinates differ.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.heightStr: The height-strip formula uses F/(c−o)+(z−o)(∂F/∂z)/(c−o), multiplied by a radial test and its supplied radial weight. Its sign specifies the orientation of the two height faces.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.presMode: The pressure coefficient is (2π)⁻¹∫₀²πe^(−iκnφ)P(r,φ,z)dφ. It transforms only the spatial angle and leaves r and z fixed.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.quadFormV: The quadratic value is Re(u*Φu), with conjugation on the first vector. A Hermitian matrix is an additional assumption when that property is needed.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.radialStr: The radial trace moment is represented by a strip integral of F/(c−o)+(r−o)∂ᵣF/(c−o), with the orientation sign and the height test. The width c−o must be nonzero for the trace interpretation.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.radialWei: The primitive is ∫₀ʳρt(ρ)dρ, retaining the cylindrical factor ρ used in the trace identities.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.Exterior.traceFreeCon: The contraction constant is exactly √(7/2). Subsequent estimates may replace it by a larger upper bound.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.Finite.quadValue: The value is xᵀMx for a real matrix M and a real vector x. Symmetry and nonnegativity require additional hypotheses on M.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.FracCellData: The steady data are supplemented by a cell region, reference and polynomial model fields, approximation budgets, and spectral cutoffs. The associated conditions must establish the claimed bounds on these inputs.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.ChartPara: The compactified chart uses a length L, a core radius, a small auxiliary parameter ε, and an azimuthal symmetry order κ. Their sign and size conditions are imposed separately.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.IsChartPa: The chart requires L>0, a positive core radius, 0<ε<1/8, and κ>0. The final cell certificate strengthens the symmetry-order condition to κ≥3.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.IsTensorM: Both knot lists must be strictly increasing, begin at 0, and end at 1. Consequently each direction contains at least one interval.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.Spline: A spline specifies a complex bivariate polynomial for each pair of interval indices. Values beyond the active mesh range are also part of the representation.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.Spline.Va: Every polynomial whose radial left knot is at or beyond the cutoff must vanish, including all height indices. Missing radial knots are assigned value 1, so a cutoff below 1 also requires the corresponding out-of-range pieces to vanish.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.Spline.co: Conjugation leaves the spline mesh unchanged and replaces every polynomial coefficient by its complex conjugate.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.Spline.ev: Evaluation first selects the radial and height intervals and then evaluates their polynomial at the given chart coordinates. Agreement and continuity across interfaces require the joining conditions.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.TensorMes: The spline mesh consists of a radial knot list and a normalized-height knot list. Ordering and endpoint requirements are separate conditions.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.atFirst: The operation substitutes a fixed complex value for the first polynomial variable and leaves the second variable unchanged.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.atSecond: The operation substitutes a fixed complex value for the second polynomial variable and leaves the first variable unchanged.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.azimVecQ: The weighted azimuthal vector is a=(−y₂/|y|,y₁/|y|,0), with value 0 at the origin. It vanishes on the rotation axis.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.cellCount: The interval count is the number of knots minus one, with result zero for an empty list. A valid mesh has enough ordered endpoints to represent actual intervals.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.cellIndex: The selected interval is determined by the number of internal knots at or below the coordinate. At an internal knot, the piece on the right is chosen.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.chartT: The compactified radius is σ=|y|/(|y|+L), as in (B.3). It is a spatial coordinate.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.heightDer: The chart derivative is ∂η at fixed compactified radius σ. It differs from differentiating with respect to the physical height z.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.heightRat: The normalized height is η=z/|y|, assigned value 0 at y=0. The complete field conditions must supply the required regularity at the origin.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.polarVecQ: The weighted polar vector is p=(ηy₁/|y|,ηy₂/|y|,−(1−η²)). Its prescribed value at the origin is (0,0,−1); regularity is a condition on the complete field.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.qOf: The polar vanishing factor is 1−η². Away from the origin it vanishes on the rotation axis.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.radialSca: The radial scaling operator is σ(1−σ)∂σ, which equals |y|∂|y| under the compactification. Oscillatory radial phases contribute separate terms.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.radialVec: The radial chart vector is y/|y| away from the origin, with assigned value 0 at y=0. Origin conditions on the full field account for this extension.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.tDeriv: The operator takes the specified number of polynomial derivatives in the radial chart variable. Order zero leaves the polynomial unchanged.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.weightPol: The endpoint weight is σ^e₀(1−σ)^e₁ for nonnegative integers e₀ and e₁. These powers control the origin and far-field behavior.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.xDeriv: The operator takes repeated polynomial derivatives in the normalized-height variable, with the radial variable fixed.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.permSign: The alternating symbol is +1 on cyclic permutations, −1 on anticyclic permutations, and zero when an index repeats. These signs fix the orientation of the curl.
notes.Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.CellSystemCond: All fifteen conditions must hold for the same seven collections of data. They give a conditional route from those data to the certificate and do not provide a particular numerical certificate.
notes.Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.CertificateCla: These are the scalar sign, residual, contraction, parameter-inclusion and nontriviality requirements from Section 7. Positivity of the weight and periods is supplied by the other final cell conditions.
notes.Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.CoerciveNumber: The supplied numbers bound the multiplier weight, its derivative, the frequency ratio and the total cell error. The same total error is used in both the cell and assembly inequalities.
notes.Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.PotentialEntri: A potential series and chart are supplied for each coefficient index, together with one shared pin representation. Series validity is required only for active adjoint indices.
For every active adjoint, the potential and pin fields must equal the validated represented fields. Agreement of the shared pin matrix with the certificate holds for the full family.
notes.Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.ReductionEntri: The reduction data supply the profile, pressure, adjoints, offsets, shifts and potentials used to obtain the Section 7 certificate; all conditions use these same choices.
notes.Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.ShiftNumbers: The error from the fixed reference to the centre is separated from the additional change over K; the corresponding gradient bounds use L² and L³ respectively.
notes.Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.ShiftNumbersBo: At every time the centre gradient error has an L² bound and the parameter-dependent gradient error has an L³ bound, both using the operator norm. Their weighted sums control the linearization gap and the frozen-form shift.
notes.Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.breakdownOnSpa: One set of data satisfying all fifteen cell conditions yields both the whole-space and periodic nonexistence conclusions. This implication remains conditional on the data satisfying those conditions.

If all fifteen cell conditions hold, every positive viscosity admits smooth compactly supported divergence-free initial data on ℝ³ with no global smooth bounded-energy solution. The readable file states this implication; its proof belongs to the separate proof library.
notes.Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.breakdownOnTor: If all fifteen cell conditions hold, every positive viscosity admits smooth periodic divergence-free data with no global smooth solution preserving the velocity periodicity, allowing any smooth pressure. The readable file states the implication, whose proof is supplied separately.
notes.Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.Ad: The adjoint, pin coefficients, centre, tangent fields and reciprocal-period rates must agree across the supplied data. Every fitted-direction set is empty on this cell route.
All adjoint harmonics share one chart and phase, with a separate finite harmonic field for each adjoint index.
notes.Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.In: The profile, pressure and adjoint representation conditions must hold together, tying the analytic fields to the supplied harmonic data.
notes.Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.Is: Every active adjoint equals its represented field for all α, hence is parameter independent. Each of its active harmonics has decay exponent at least 3.
The reciprocal period and forcing coefficients are affine on K. Certified core pairing errors and uniform exterior norm bounds then determine the offset bound by an exact equality.

The pressure coefficients satisfy conjugation, reflection, continuity and decay h≥2, together with the separate axis and origin requirements. For nonzero angular modes, origin regularity permits a positive radial power or exact vanishing of the boundary value.
For every α, time and point, the prescribed pressure gradient equals ∇(qα−|Wα|²/2).
The approximate velocity and its supplied Hessian equal the represented fields for every α, including values outside K. The target pin values are exactly the pairings with the profile gradient.
The cutoff joins through two derivatives, vanishes up to an interior breakpoint σχ and equals one near the endpoint 1.
notes.Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.Of: The data supply affine reciprocal-period and force coefficients, approximations to the constant, linear and quadratic offset pairings, their errors and exterior norm bounds.
The constant residual is evaluated with the original radial phase and centre origin profile, appropriate to the ball where the moving phase vanishes.
The linear residual uses the original phase, the tangent's own origin profile, and the corresponding tangent pressure and force.
In the ordered quadratic term, i determines the reciprocal-period rate and advecting field, while l determines the field being differentiated.
A diagonal quadratic coefficient uses one ordered term; a mixed coefficient adds both orders and then appears once in the sum over i≤l.
notes.Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.Pr: A finite harmonic set and scalar spline amplitudes specify the pressure correction with the same time, angular and radial phase conventions as the velocity.
A pressure amplitude has separate radial factors at the origin and infinity, an angular vanishing factor and a spline; the exponents are checked by the pressure conditions.
The centre and tangent pressure amplitudes are supplied separately; their shared radial phase can depend on α.
The pressure correction combines q⁰+Σᵢαᵢqⁱ after each term has been evaluated with the phase belonging to α.
The profile data supply a common chart and phase, a radial cutoff and its parameter rates, together with separate centre and tangent harmonics and origin profiles.
Both the centre and tangent fields use the phase selected by α, so the resulting family need not be affine in α outside the fixed-phase core.
The proposed radius is rχ=Lσχ/(1−σχ). With valid cutoff data and L>0, the moving phase vanishes inside this radius and parameter dependence there comes only from the affine amplitudes.
The moving phase integral uses the chosen chart length L and cutoff χ of this profile family.
At parameter α the radial phase is f+(k·α)f_*; the remaining chart data are unchanged.
The Hessian expression uses the same moved phase and the same centre and tangent amplitudes as the approximate velocity.
notes.Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.St: The radial cutoff χ is specified by its breakpoints and one polynomial for each interval; joining and cutoff requirements are separate conditions.
The value of χ is the polynomial assigned to the interval containing the argument, with the interval convention also fixing values at breakpoints.
notes.Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.af: For fixed chart and phase, the field is W⁰+ΣᵢαᵢWⁱ. Choosing the phase from α introduces additional parameter dependence.
The supplied Hessian is combined with the same centre and tangent coefficients as the velocity field; any moving phase enters before this combination.
notes.Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.ba: The pairing is integrated over one normalized period and the closed ball of radius rχ. For integrable fields the sphere has zero volume, so the value agrees with the open-ball pairing in the paper.
notes.Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.ce: The constant residual coefficient contains the time and similarity terms, diffusion, convection, the central force and ∇(q⁰−|W⁰|²/2).
notes.Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.co: For j∈J the coordinate bound is its box radius; on the complementary coordinates it is |ϱ_*|/|dᵢ|. The certificate conditions ensure those denominators are nonzero.
notes.Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.li: The linear coefficient includes the two time contributions, both mixed convection terms, the tangent force and −∇(W⁰·Wⁱ) in the pressure adjustment.
notes.Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.mo: The radial phase f is replaced by f+af_* while the chart length, symmetry order and origin profile stay fixed.
notes.Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.of: The offset bound adds the constant error, linear errors after subtracting dⱼ on the diagonal, quadratic errors with i≤l, and the product of the exterior residual and adjoint bounds.
notes.Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.ph: The scalar phase displacement is k·α=Σᵢkᵢαᵢ, as in the moving phase of (B.9).
notes.Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.pr: One pressure term is its phase multiplied by σ^{h₀}(1−σ)^h(1−η²)^{h′₀} and the scalar spline amplitude.
The centre field uses its own origin profile and the phase fα, so the centre can depend on α even though its harmonic amplitudes are fixed.
Each tangent retains its own amplitudes and origin profile while being evaluated with the common moved phase fα.
notes.Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.qu: The ordered quadratic term uses the period rate of direction i and the derivative of direction l. A mixed coefficient is obtained by adding the two orders.
notes.Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.sh: The correction q is the real part of the finite pressure harmonic sum. The pressure gradient used in the residual is subsequently adjusted by −∇(|W|²/2).
notes.Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.st: The moving phase is f_*(s)=∫₀^{√s}χ(r/(r+L))dr/r. Vanishing of χ near zero removes the singularity in this integral for valid cutoff data.
notes.Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.ti: This is differentiation in the normalized time θ at fixed y; multiplication by the reciprocal period occurs in the residual expansion.
notes.Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.wi: Each centre or tangent field can have its own origin profile g while sharing the chart, angular symmetry and radial phase.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.AdmissibleTuple: An admissible collection contains v, its weak derivatives, the time-and-dilation derivative, forcing coefficients and an L² right-hand side. The positive density must be finite for the explicitly chosen form coefficient.

notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.CellVars: The full cell vector includes polynomial and trace coordinates, auxiliary ports, forcing coefficients and pin coefficients.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.ConjDatum: Conjugate coordinates have opposite angular modes and matching components, polynomial degrees and geometry. The relevant interval, corner or basis data must also agree.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.CouplingEntr: For each cell, the potential and finite pairing data are supplied together on the same cell coordinates.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.EliminationC: The matrix comparison holds on the specified admissible cell vectors, with positive gradient weights, excluded singular angular modes and the stated slack and row-matrix conditions. In the final certificate those vectors are exactly the permitted global row representations.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.EntryCharges: On each cell one bound controls all harmonic charges and the reciprocal lower bound for the length, together with the required measurability.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.ExteriorCove: The exterior cover combines finitely many ray-integrated and pointwise regions, with one common charge family and a selection of regions for each harmonic.
The selected exterior condition supplies its harmonic set, which may be infinite.
The exterior region is taken from whichever ray or pointwise condition is selected.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.FarFieldCond: The chart bounds agree with the exterior charges and control the reference field at every time and angle. The length is positive and common to all harmonics on the exterior.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.FarFieldValu: The exterior data supply chart-based bounds for the strain, mean vorticity gradient and oscillatory vorticity gradient.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.FieldRegular: The reference field has a weak Hessian and the stated harmonic expansion, and its multiplier data are admissible and measurable. The forcing fields also satisfy their analytic harmonic conditions.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.FluxChoice: The flux data supply the symmetry choice and optional real and imaginary stream values at both endpoints; the subsequent conditions establish the moment identity.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.InRowRange: Used cell coordinates are reconstructed from one real global vector plus arbitrary complex gauge and constant-pressure directions. Unused coordinates and ports remain free, while forcing and pin coordinates are real.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.IsBoundedOnC: The field must be measurable up to a null set and bounded at every point of the closed cell rectangle by a finite constant.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.IsExteriorCo: For each harmonic the selected regions cover the exterior in the quarter plane, lie within it and overlap only on null sets. Every stored condition is valid, and the common charges satisfy the stated measurability and boundedness requirements.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.IsKeyEvaluat: A coordinate may be read directly, conjugated, reflected on z=0, or both conjugated and reflected. Reflection uses the prescribed parity and requires the coordinate to lie on that plane.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.IsKeyVar: A common boundary unknown must have the stated harmonic, boundary coordinate and real or imaginary part, without a separate cell or forcing-coordinate assignment.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.IsOffModeCov: For every non-resolved harmonic, including eliminated harmonics, the selected conditions cover the positive-radius part of the cell, contain that harmonic and dominate the required charges.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.IsRegionChar: The regional estimates bound the strain, mean vorticity gradient and its oscillatory remainder. The length parameter is positive and common to all harmonic labels in the region.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.KeyEvaluatio: The proposed reading specifies a harmonic, a choice of complex conjugation and a real sign; the symmetry conditions restrict it to the four allowed cases.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.OffModeCover: A finite family of regional conditions is supplied, and each cell and integer harmonic selects a finite subfamily to cover its unresolved estimate.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.PairingCondi: The retained pairing matrix is bounded on the permitted cell vectors, and nonzero pairing profiles have the required tail or full-profile Gram estimates. Those estimates quantify real forcing and pin coefficients.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.PairingData: The pairing data provide a finite harmonic set, proposed positive weights and Gram matrices controlling tails of the profile weighted by β and 2ζ.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.PartBound: A present component must refer to the matching real global unknown. An absent component needs a valid omission condition or a stream value at the axis.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.PotentialCon: The potential conditions require the retained-matrix estimate, harmonic coverage, absorption budgets and analytic regularity together. The form estimates use the same permitted cell vectors as the global row construction.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.PotentialDat: The potential data specify the model convolution, a matrix splitting the retained coordinates, harmonic groups and the lengths and weights used in the error estimates. These values require the subsequent compatibility inequalities.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowCondition: Rows enumerate every harmonic-test pair exactly once, with positive Gram and leakage weights. Their matrix bound includes both resolved polynomial tails and unresolved leakage contributions.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry: Each row has finite support, complex coefficients, a specified justification and a rank ordering its dependencies. Separate selections identify forcing, pin and port unknowns.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.Acc: The stated justification for a row determines the complete set of equalities, geometric conditions and dependency checks that it must satisfy.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.Der: The relation combination has coefficient 1 at the target and coefficient 0 at every pressure coordinate. Every other nonzero term uses an available row of smaller rank, giving a terminating reconstruction.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.Flu: Radial and horizontal faces use their respective stream-flux identities. The horizontal case also uses a valid linear velocity moment of strictly smaller dependency rank.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.Key: A shared-coordinate row must have an allowed symmetry reading, valid real and imaginary components and the exact resulting row coefficients; private interior coordinates are excluded.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.Lea: A directly read cell coordinate must supply its real component and may supply its imaginary component. Omitting the imaginary part is allowed only for the zero harmonic.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.Nor: The normal-derivative row follows from divergence freedom, differentiated polynomial tests and endpoint velocities. The lower endpoint may be omitted only where a horizontal face starts at the axis.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.Spl: The intervals form a nonempty consecutive subdivision with exact polynomial test expansions, valid shared coordinates and justified flux substitutions. Their weighted sum must equal the original row exactly.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.Unu: An unused coordinate has a zero reconstruction row, zero row and column in the cell matrix and no use in a rectangle credit.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.cor: All three velocity components at the corner must be available at strictly smaller dependency rank.
A present corner supplies its velocity row; an absent corner contributes the zero row.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.rel: The coefficient is the finite weighted sum of the chosen cell-relation coefficients at the selected coordinate.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.row: The cell embedding combines the reconstructed rows, complex ports and the forcing and pin selections. If two port contributions select the same unknown their coefficients are added.
The row value is the finite sum of its complex coefficients multiplied by the corresponding real global unknowns.
Only coefficients inside the declared finite support are retained; the row is zero outside that support.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.til: The constant normal-velocity moment is recovered from endpoint stream values. The radial formula divides by the face radius, and the horizontal formula uses the nonzero leading coefficient of the linear test.
One subdivision segment uses its own endpoints and test coefficients at the fixed level of the original face.
The endpoint-flux formula is used only for the constant moment of a tile designated for that substitution; other tile moments use their direct real and imaginary coordinates.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.vel: A usable velocity trace has an allowed degree, a dependency rank below the target and a justification that uses the coordinate.
A velocity-trace row is returned for degrees in the specified range; beyond that range its value is zero.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowFunctiona: The row identities must reproduce the tested equation, including the eliminated modes and polynomial remainders. Harmonic coverage and the error budgets must hold with the same data and uniformly over K where parameters occur.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowReason: A row has one of seven justifications: shared boundary data, subdivision, a flux identity, a relation, a normal-derivative identity, direct cell data or absence from all relevant forms.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowReason.Is: This marks a row as unused. The separate unused-row conditions require its coefficients and all matrix and credit contributions to vanish.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.SplitChoice: The subdivision data supply interval endpoints, local tests, polynomial expansion coefficients and optional direct or stream coordinates; their consistency is checked by the subdivision conditions.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.TailConditio: Each resolved harmonic's tail budget must agree with the leaf's high-derivative lower bounds and cover all allocated costs. The high-degree correction matrix is their exact weighted sum.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.TreeRowCondi: The tree embedding equals the constructed rows, the global form satisfies its one-sided upper bound, and constant-pressure directions are annihilated. The chosen base perturbation, its derivative fields, forcing coefficients and right-hand side vanish on K.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.absorbValue: The resolved low profile is inserted into the leaf's three absorption terms for curl, gradient and velocity.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.activeGroups: A group is active for a row when one of its row partners differs from that row by a harmonic in the group.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.actuatorRow: The forcing row is the integral of its harmonic against the conjugated vector test, with the cylindrical factor r.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.bandEliminat: The eliminated-mode term integrates a square-completion expression with measure r dr dz. When its slack is zero, a separate exact identity forces the divided remainder to vanish.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.bandGram: The eliminated-row Gram matrix integrates the conjugated product of transformed row fields with the radial measure and inverse gradient weights.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.bandPart: The selected part is Px. Together with x−Px it reconstructs the original cell vector exactly.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.couplingPair: All resolved harmonic pairs are integrated with coupling label ι−ι′ and radial measure r dr dz, fixing the convolution order.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.couplingTail: The coupling tail is the remainder after polynomial projection at degree Q for gradient components and degree Q−1 for velocity components. It contains both the model convolution and the same-harmonic local matrix action.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.creditVelDem: The velocity charge sums the rectangle weights where the harmonic equals the reflected rectangle harmonic or its negative and the point lies in that rectangle.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.crossTest: The twelve-component test combines the velocity and vorticity cross-product contributions, with the written conjugations fixing the complex pairing convention.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.deactSources: The possible inactive sources are all tested-harmonic minus reference-harmonic differences lying outside both the resolved and eliminated sets.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.epsOwnCharge: The local model-error charge splits into curl, gradient and velocity squares with the specified strain and vorticity-gradient errors and two length parameters.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.gradOf: Gradient entry (a,b) occupies position 3a+b among the first nine entries, fixing the matrix component convention.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.gradSlot: The gradient occupies the first nine positions of the twelve-component vector, followed by the three velocity components.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.groupCharge: A group's gradient and velocity costs are balanced using its vorticity-gradient bound, matrix constant and length; the curl cost uses its strain bound.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.headUnit: The constant-pressure direction is inserted in one harmonic's cell coordinates and is zero on all other harmonics, ports and coefficient groups.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.highOwnAmoun: The high-component charge is integrated with radial measure over the cell and summed over the chosen finite harmonic set.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.highOwnCharg: The high-component error is distributed among curl, full-gradient and velocity squares using three positive balancing weights.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.isPressureDa: The test recognizes precisely the pressure-trace coordinates among the eight cell coordinate families.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.keyFlipSign: Velocity and corner values use the frame reflection sign, normal-gradient values use its negative, pressure uses +1 and the stream value uses the vertical sign.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.keyOnPlane: A plane coordinate lies on a horizontal face at z=0 or at a corner or stream point of that plane. Private coordinates are excluded.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.keyVelNormal: The test selects the normal component of a zero-angular velocity trace, whose flux can be recovered from endpoint stream values.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.keyWithMode: The angular mode is replaced in velocity, gradient, pressure and corner coordinates while their geometry is retained; stream and private coordinates are unchanged.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.leakGram: The leakage Gram matrix uses the harmonic leakage weight as the divisor of each row Gram block.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.linearField: The resulting field is a finite complex linear combination of the supplied coefficient fields; its input coefficients are used without conjugation.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.longFactor: For |ι₁| at or below the cutoff the factor is the chosen balance t; above it the factor is 1+1/t.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.longOwnCharg: The long-component strain and vorticity-gradient charge is multiplied by the appropriate factor on each side of the angular cutoff.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.longRowCost: The row cost is chosen from its low or high value according to the absolute angular label and the long-component cutoff.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.longRowTerm: The long-component contribution is zero when both velocity and vorticity errors are exactly zero. Otherwise it is the reciprocal of the selected row cost.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.longSourceCo: A low source uses the high cost; a high source uses the sum of the low and high costs.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.lowAt: The low profile is used on resolved harmonics and extended by zero at every other harmonic.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.lowGrad: The low gradient is the sum of the polynomial gradient reconstructions over the internal angular modes of the chosen resolved harmonic.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.lowProfile: The local vector places nine gradient entries first and three velocity entries last, matching the order of the 12×12 matrices.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.lowVel: The low velocity is obtained by summing the corresponding polynomial velocity reconstructions over the internal angular modes.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.modelBilin: The expression expands the strain and vorticity-gradient contributions using two velocity-gradient pairs and the alternating symbol; neither pair is conjugated here.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.modelLabels: A declared model harmonic is retained only if at least one of its velocity, vorticity, strain or vorticity-gradient components is nonzero somewhere on the cell.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.modelTriple: Averaging the model expression with its two velocity-gradient pairs exchanged makes it symmetric in those pairs; complex conjugation is handled separately.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.modelVelocit: The vector consists of the three components of the chosen velocity-model harmonic at the given meridian point.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.modelVortici: The vector consists of the corresponding three components of the vorticity-model harmonic.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.pairArray: The same matrix entries are indexed by a pair (a,b); their order and values are unchanged.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.pairWeightOf: The forcing coefficients enter with weight β, while the pin coefficients enter with weight 2ζ.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.pairingExact: The finite pairing integrates resolved gradients against that weighted profile and subtracts a Gram penalty for each selected error harmonic.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.pairingProfi: The pairing profile is the complex linear combination of the forcing-gradient and pin profiles with weights β and 2ζ.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.partVec: The row adds its optional real coefficient and ±i times its optional imaginary coefficient, with the minus sign used under conjugation. Both contributions remain if they select the same unknown.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.potentialExa: The potential expression combines the complementary-complementary and twice the complementary-selected interactions, then subtracts local, port, group and approximation costs. notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.presUnitMome: The pressure-trace coordinate receives the face moment of constant pressure under the specified harmonic convention; every other coordinate receives zero.

notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.restrictData: Restriction to one resolved harmonic reads that harmonic's polynomial and trace coordinates, leaving out ports and global coefficient groups.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.retileKey: Retiling a face changes its interval, test polynomials and degree while retaining the physical quantity, angular mode and orientation.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.rowBaseWeigh: The base row weight divides each Gram block by the test weight assigned to that harmonic.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.rowCrossTest: The model harmonic is the row harmonic minus the source harmonic, and it is paired with that row's polynomial test.

notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.testAt: The stored polynomial test component is evaluated on the chosen physical cell.

notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.totalStrainC: The total gradient cost is the sum of the potential, pairing and tested-row costs for the chosen harmonic.

notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Bridge.IsCreditPatch: The same tests and matrices must satisfy the trace identity, weighted Dirichlet bound and inverse-matrix comparison. The charge bounds and Lipschitz bounds hold globally, while the energy comparison is integrated over the rectangle.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Bridge.IsCrossWaveEnt: For every point in the region, every angle, and every complex vector, the reconstructed symmetric strain and vorticity-gradient operators obey their squared norm bounds. The balancing parameters must also be positive.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Bridge.IsHarmonicExpa: A finite set closed under negation reconstructs the field, its spatial gradient, and the supplied Hessian exactly at every time and point. The asserted identities concern the full functions.

notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.BoxConst: The auxiliary numbers specify the source and length weights, strain allowance, per-harmonic row weights and orthogonal-tail weight used to allocate approximation errors.

notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.sideGrad: The gradient boundary row has the negative outward-normal sign; a radial face also supplies its fixed radial coordinate.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.sidePres: The pressure boundary row has the outward-normal sign and pairs with the radial or vertical test component according to the face orientation.

notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.testValu: The three polynomial test components are evaluated in the coordinates of the selected cell.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.turnVect: For angular wave number k the frame derivative sends (xᵣ,xφ,x_z) to (ikxᵣ−xφ,ikxφ+xᵣ,ikx_z).
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.velAt: This is the selected cylindrical component of a velocity harmonic at the given meridian point.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.vorticit: Contracting the supplied Hessian with the curl coefficients gives the vorticity gradient, so the expression also applies to the chosen weak-Hessian representative.

notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellHypothesis: The cell hypothesis joins seventeen requirements, including the tree, model, trace and support conditions and the fixed values 39/50, 3/50 and 1000. It supplies the first of the fifteen final certificate conditions.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellLayerData: The cell data join the extended certificate, multiplier pieces, harmonic bounds, reference field, mesh, rows, models, pins, and coercivity constants. Their compatibility is established by the fifteen certificate conditions.

notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellLayerData.labelDe: The reduced mode density uses the parameter's period, weights, and harmonic bounds at normalized time zero and angle zero. The cylindrical factor r is inserted when integrating it.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellLayerData.pinFiel: The pinning tensor Ξᵢ is obtained by evaluating its cell-polynomial matrix coefficients with the chosen symmetry order. Its pairing with a perturbation is defined separately.

notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellLayerData.withFor: Only the form coefficient c in the multiplier pieces is replaced; the other cell data, including the separately specified coercivity value, are retained.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellLayerEntries: The same witnesses supply local matrices, coupling data, unresolved and exterior covers, exterior enclosures and global rows throughout the assembly conditions.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellLayerEntryConditi: Twenty requirements join the local forms, tested rows, exterior bounds and tree. The form inequalities share the same permitted row vectors, and separate annihilation conditions control pressure and gauge directions.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellMatField: For each cell, the matrix data specify active harmonics and a polynomial for each ordered pair of cylindrical components. Coefficients outside the active set do not enter the field sum.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellMatField.IsConjug: The active matrix labels are closed under negation and reflection, and opposite labels have conjugate component polynomials for every label. These conditions alone impose no derivative relation with a vector field.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellMatField.field: The matrix field sums the real harmonic matrices in the cylindrical frame on each closed cell solid. The same cell indicators are used as for the vector fields.

notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellMatField.planeVal: Matrix reflection multiplies an entry by the signs of both cylindrical indices. Exactly one radial index gives a minus sign.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellMesh: The mesh data specify rectangles, resolved and tested harmonics, eliminated harmonics, and polynomial degrees for each cell and label. The geometry and compatibility of these choices are imposed by later conditions.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellMesh.closedHalfPl: The closed meridian quadrant is {(r,z):r≥0,z≥0}, including both coordinate boundaries.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellMesh.exterior: The exterior consists of the closed meridian quadrant with the cell region removed. The mode integrals are subsequently taken over the open quarter-plane.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellMesh.maxVolumeDeg: The maximum volume degree is taken over the resolved labels of the cell. It is assigned value zero when that set is empty.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellMesh.region: The cell region is the union of all stored closed rectangles. It is empty when there are no cells.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellPoly: The polynomial data give a degree bound d in each affine cell coordinate and a square (d+1)×(d+1) complex coefficient array. Leading coefficients may vanish.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellPoly.eval: The cell polynomial is evaluated in the affine coordinates ξ and η of the meridian rectangle. Coefficients given instead in powers of r and z require a change of basis.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellPoly.scale: Scaling a polynomial multiplies all its coefficients by one complex scalar while retaining its degree bound.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellPoly.zero: The chosen zero polynomial has degree bound zero and its single coefficient is zero. Other all-zero coefficient arrays evaluate to the same function.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellVecField: For each cell, the vector data specify a finite set of active harmonics and three component polynomials. Only the active harmonic set contributes to the evaluated field.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellVecField.IsConjug: Active vector harmonics are closed under negation and reflection. For every label, including labels outside the active set, the coefficient at −ι is the complex conjugate of the coefficient at ι.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellVecField.field: The field sums the real harmonic components in the cylindrical frame over the closed solid of every cell. Shared boundaries can receive multiple terms, while valid cell overlaps have zero measure.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellVecField.planeVal: The vector coefficient at negative height uses the reflected label with signs +1, −1, −1 for its three cylindrical components. At nonnegative height it uses the given polynomial directly.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.ComplexNo: The complex node data additionally specify the map from real coordinates, a scaling factor, and separate positive and negative complex column families. Each negative column yields a real and an imaginary global column.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.Coordinat: Each complex coordinate is formed from an optional real coordinate and an optional signed imaginary coordinate. Shared global coordinates are permitted unless additional conditions exclude them.
A real coordinate belongs to a complex coordinate when it is selected as either its real part or its imaginary part.

notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.IsCoordin: On the pivot set, the imaginary sign satisfies s²=1, and a present real coordinate cannot also be the imaginary coordinate of the same pivot. The condition applies only to pivots.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.PassesCom: The complex node enclosure uses Hermitian matrices and weighted residual moduli, then transfers the resulting bounds to real coordinates. notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.PassesNod: A node is accepted when either a real enclosure or a complex enclosure exists, together with the data and error matrices for that branch. Each branch uses one consistent choice of those data.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.PassesPiv: Every prescribed or free coordinate must be pivoted with positive slack, and the root front must have a nonnegative quadratic form. The total number of indexed negative columns is at most the number of free coordinates.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.PassesRea: The real node enclosure bounds its input and outgoing forms with nonnegative symmetric error matrices and a weighted absolute row-sum bound. At a pivot, the available tree slack is bounded by the pivot value minus its error radius.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.RealNodeD: The real node data specify approximate input and outgoing matrices, pivot values, scaling weights, error radii, and positive factor columns. The node-enclosure conditions establish symmetry and the required inequalities.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.SignedTre: The assembly data specify finitely many leaf forms, nodes, and negative columns, together with their placements, parent links, fronts, pivots, and slacks. Additional conditions govern the parent relation.

A node receives the leaf forms assigned to it and the outgoing fronts of all nodes whose parent is that node. The sum uses the stated parent relation directly.

notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.slackRema: The real residual is M−diag(δ)−F₊F₊ᵀ+F₋F₋ᵀ−S. The diagonal is supported only on the selected pivots.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CoefficientConditions: Every harmonic and every point of the quarter plane must be covered by the appropriate coefficient lower bound, including points outside the mesh. The velocity lower bound is weighted by r²+z².
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CoefficientEntry: A finite list of coefficient enclosures is paired with mode sets and spatial regions, which can themselves be infinite. Additional lower coefficients are supplied for resolved and eliminated harmonics.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.ContinuumConditionsGi: Three common enclosure constants work uniformly on K, reflection identities hold, and one coefficient-enclosure family covers the required modes and regions.

notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Coupling.quadForm: The complex matrix form is Re(x*Ax), using the standard conjugate pairing.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Coupling.realQuadForm: A real matrix acts on complex coordinates after its entries are regarded as complex numbers, and the real part of x*Ax is taken.

notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CreditEval.IsPlaneSid: The selected trace is a vertical-velocity moment on z=0, with the prescribed interval and test function and the cell on its positive-height side.

notes.Breakdown.CertCell.GaugeKey.KeyInHalfPla: Radial faces and corners must have positive radius; horizontal intervals and stream points may reach radius zero. Private interior coordinates impose no boundary-location condition.
