notes.Breakdown.CertCell.frameSign: The reflected cylindrical components have signs +1, −1, −1 in the radial, azimuthal, and axial directions.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.frameUnit: The moving frame is ordered as (eᵣ,eφ,e_z). Vector and matrix components use this order.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.globalForm: The global form is −(cM²/(4π)+e)|β|²−|ζ|²/(4πs). The cell conditions later set c=3/50 and s=1000.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.halfPlane: The analytic meridian domain is {(r,z):r>0,z>0}. The axis and symmetry plane are excluded from these area integrals.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.keySeg: The boundary segment retains its level, endpoints and test coefficients; its auxiliary opposite level is assigned one unit above the given level.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.labelAzimuth: The angular integer associated with ι is κι₁, as in (B.2).
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.labelFlip: Reflection sends ι to (−ι₁,ι₂−ι₁). It reverses the angular frequency and preserves the temporal frequency.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.labelGrad: The gradient coefficient is evaluated on the same time-zero, angle-zero meridian plane. Its two indices retain the gradient component convention used by the mode transform.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.labelHarmonic: The lattice label ι corresponds to the temporal-angular frequency pair (2ι₂−ι₁,κι₁).
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.labelPhase: The harmonic is Eι(θ,φ)=exp(i[2π(2ι₂−ι₁)θ+κι₁φ]). Here θ is normalized time and φ is the spatial angle.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.labelTime: The temporal integer associated with ι is 2ι₂−ι₁. It multiplies 2π times the normalized time in (B.2).
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.labelValueAt: At negative height, the coefficient is evaluated at reflected height using the reflected lattice label and the specified component sign. This operation preserves temporal frequency.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.labelVel: The velocity coefficient uses the harmonic associated with ι and is evaluated at normalized time zero and angle zero. Its three entries are the cylindrical components on the meridian plane.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.planePoint: The meridian point (r,z) is placed at (r,0,z), the spatial point of angle zero.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.pointAngle: The angle is the argument of y₁+iy₂. Integer angular harmonics make the choice of argument branch consistent away from the axis, while axis regularity belongs to the complete field conditions.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.pointPlane: The meridian coordinates of a spatial point are (√(y₁²+y₂²),y₃), retaining the sign of the height.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.realLeafForm: The real matrix is Re(P*ΨP), the complex form transferred by P to the real global coordinates.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.rowPartFactor: Multiplication by 1 preserves the real part, while multiplication by −i makes the real part equal the original imaginary part.
notes.Breakdown.CertReduction.AdjointQuadNumbe: For each adjoint, the data choose an L³ or L² estimate and provide a proposed norm bound; the associated validity condition supplies nonnegativity and the actual bound.
notes.Breakdown.CertReduction.AdjointQuadratic: For each j∈J, a nonnegative bound controls the selected adjoint norm at every time and every α∈K, and its weighted coefficient is at most ãⱼ.
notes.Breakdown.CertReduction.AdjointSizeBound: The chosen inequality bounds either ∫|ψ|³ by n³ or ∫|ψ|² by n². Nonnegativity of n is imposed separately when these inequalities are used.
notes.Breakdown.CertReduction.FrozenFormBounde: Uniformly in α and time, the symmetric gradient is bounded below as a quadratic form and the cube of its operator norm is integrable. Their stated combination must fit within the frozen-form bound.
notes.Breakdown.CertReduction.ModelFormNumbers: The two proposed numbers are the lower strain bound s₋ and an L³ bound for the reference gradient, used to control the frozen quadratic form.
notes.Breakdown.CertReduction.adjointQuadCoeff: The quadratic adjoint coefficient is 2/(√3w_*) in the L³ case and c_w/√w_* in the L² case, before multiplication by the adjoint norm bound.
notes.Breakdown.CertReduction.gapGradCoeff: The gradient contribution to the profile gap uses either 2/(√3√w_*) with an L³ bound or the weighted supremum constant c_w with an L² bound.
notes.Breakdown.CertReduction.shiftGradCoeff: The L³ contribution to the quadratic-form shift is 1/(√3√w_*), half its contribution to the profile gap; the alternative L² coefficient is c_w.
notes.Breakdown.PotentialShape.AxisCellsVanish: All angular coefficients affecting either endpoint cell must vanish. This can supply axis regularity in place of an explicit positive axis power.
notes.Breakdown.PotentialShape.CylModeData: A finite harmonic set is supplied with three cylindrical Hermite amplitudes per harmonic; the field formula adds one factor of the cylindrical radius.
notes.Breakdown.PotentialShape.EndVanishOrder: At the final compactified radial breakpoint, all derivative coefficients below the specified order vanish for every angular coefficient.
notes.Breakdown.PotentialShape.IsCylModeData: The support radius is positive and smaller than the mesh radius; its positive and negative boundaries are mesh knots, and every active amplitude satisfies the coefficient vanishing conditions.
notes.Breakdown.PotentialShape.IsJetMesh: The breakpoints must be strictly ordered with the prescribed first and last values. No matching of derivatives across intervals is required by this mesh condition alone.
notes.Breakdown.PotentialShape.IsPinShapeEntry: The pin mesh, cylindrical supports, generator shapes and support breakpoints must be valid. Agreement with the certificate's matrix field is an additional condition.
notes.Breakdown.PotentialShape.IsPotentialScal: The amplitude has first-order joining in both variables, and its required origin and infinity orders may be split between explicit powers and vanishing endpoint derivatives.
notes.Breakdown.PotentialShape.IsPotentialSeri: The vector potentials have the required first-order joining and radial decay, the matrix potential joins in its normal directions, and the pressure meets its separate axis and origin conditions. These are sufficient conditions for the analytic estimates of (B.51).
notes.Breakdown.PotentialShape.PinShapeEntry: The pin data supply cylindrical potentials Φₗ, proposed generators Φ̃ₗ and cell matrix fields. Compact support and the equalities tying these representations together are required separately.
notes.Breakdown.PotentialShape.PinShapeEntry.p: The two pin families are obtained by evaluating the supplied cylindrical-potential and generator representations. Compact support of the generators is required separately.
The pin matrix is evaluated on the specified mesh at its symmetry order; a separate equality identifies it with the certificate's pin matrix.
notes.Breakdown.PotentialShape.PotComponent: The potential is represented by the circular components x+iy and x−iy and its vertical component, each with its own angular frequency shift.
notes.Breakdown.PotentialShape.PotComponent.ca: Both circular components receive the polar factor √(1−η²); the vertical component receives no extra sine factor.
notes.Breakdown.PotentialShape.PotComponent.sh: The angular frequency is shifted by +1 for x+iy, by −1 for x−iy and by zero for the vertical component.
notes.Breakdown.PotentialShape.PotKeyData: For each harmonic the amplitudes specify G, U, the radial and polar parts of the matrix potential F, and the scalar q.
notes.Breakdown.PotentialShape.PotScalar: A scalar potential combines a tensor Hermite amplitude with explicit origin, infinity and axis factors. Vanishing endpoint derivatives can contribute additional radial order.
notes.Breakdown.PotentialShape.PotentialSeries: Only the harmonics in the supplied finite set contribute to the potential, even though amplitudes can be specified for other harmonics as well.
The represented G, U, matrix potential and pressure are collected as four fields. Their analytic properties require the separate potential conditions.
notes.Breakdown.PotentialShape.StartRowConstan: The initial radial row has zero angular derivative and bubble coefficients, and every angular node value in that row is equal to one common constant.
notes.Breakdown.PotentialShape.StartVanishOrde: At the first radial breakpoint, all derivative coefficients below the specified order vanish for every angular coefficient.
notes.Breakdown.PotentialShape.VanishesBeyond: Node and bubble coefficients outside the support radius must vanish in both coordinates, including the indicated endpoint cases. The requirements range over all indices, with absent breakpoints assigned the support radius.
notes.Breakdown.PotentialShape.componentValue: Each circular or vertical component uses its corresponding angular frequency shift and polar-sine factor in the scalar harmonic formula.
notes.Breakdown.PotentialShape.coordsOfCompone: Cartesian components are recovered as (g₊+g₋)/2, (g₊−g₋)/(2i) and g_z.
notes.Breakdown.PotentialShape.cylField: Each harmonic is the real part of its phase times r and its spline amplitude, multiplied by the corresponding rotating cylindrical basis vector.
notes.Breakdown.PotentialShape.dofMeetsEndCell: A coefficient touches an end cell when its node or bubble index lies in the stated first or last range; when N=0 the lower threshold N−1 is taken as zero.
notes.Breakdown.PotentialShape.fluxEntry: The flux entry is the real part of the summed harmonic contribution, with a denoting the output component and i the input direction.
notes.Breakdown.PotentialShape.fluxMap: The matrix acts on a vector by its output-by-input entries. This orientation gives the transposed matrix potential appearing in the paper's div Fᵀ convention.
notes.Breakdown.PotentialShape.fluxVector: For one harmonic and output component, the flux combines the radial and polar direction vectors with their respective scalar amplitudes.
notes.Breakdown.PotentialShape.polarSine: The polar sine is √(1−η²), where η is the Cartesian height divided by the radius; its assigned value at the origin follows the chosen coordinate convention.
notes.Breakdown.PotentialShape.pressureValue: The scalar pressure sum uses the original azimuthal frequency without a component shift or extra sine factor, and its real part is retained.
notes.Breakdown.PotentialShape.scalarValue: The scalar harmonic combines its time, azimuthal and radial phases with radial powers, an axis factor and the spline value. A separate choice adds the polar sine.
notes.Breakdown.PotentialShape.vectorPotential: The chosen G or U components are summed over the finite harmonic set, converted to Cartesian coordinates and then replaced by their real parts.
notes.Breakdown.SteadyCert.FracCertData: The data consist of steady spatial profiles, a parameter-dependent rotation rate, finite forcing and pinning families, and the constants used to bound their errors. The later time-periodic certificate supplies a separate family with a time variable.
